feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid progression at NACo. It communicates scope well, but impact would be stronger with more outcome-driven metrics, tighter formatting consistency, and less duplication across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression from coordinator to director, then consulting, which supports seniority and credibility.  
- Relevant, concrete scope: Drupal modernization, analytics stack, governance, multimedia, and AI search are all specific and aligned to the target brand.  
- Generally polished writing: concise, professional tone with good use of action verbs and credible scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes, not just responsibilities: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, production savings, adoption rates, search success, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidate to improve scannability and save space.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation around bullets/content is inconsistent; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically inconsistent with the rest; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so it would benefit from sharper differentiation and a few concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one concise value proposition plus one scope sentence; reduce the long list of functions.
- Add 1–2 scale markers already supported by the CV, e.g., “10,000+ page web platforms,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Replace “AI-enabled user experiences” with a more specific phrase like “AI-enabled search and content discovery.”
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web platforms, governance models, and content operations for complex, mission-driven organizations. Leads enterprise website transformation, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial systems, and multimedia programs—including large-scale Drupal environments serving 3.5M annual page views and 50+ publishers, as well as AI-enabled search and content discovery initiatives.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The current list mirrors Core Competencies too closely.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas with more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, category-style phrases and keep structure parallel; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experience” for clearer meaning.
- Consider “communications leadership” instead of “communications operations” to better reflect seniority.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “governance & editorial systems” vs. “multimedia production and livestream operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider reducing it to 6 items or removing any competency already named verbatim elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is already strongly established in the header and experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and foregrounding outcomes, platforms, or scope will make it more distinctive and scannable.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and separate this from core experience.
- Tighten each item to one line with a clearer lead: project + platform/channel + business purpose/outcome.
- Standardize style and wording: use parallel verbs, consistent hyphenation (“AI-enabled,” “bill-level”), and numerals (“10 x 20-foot”).
- Consider this rewrite: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search—Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat. We Are Counties Microsite—Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Developed a multi-part digital campaign spanning editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Produced a recurring advocacy video series across planning, production, and distribution for web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and Advocacy Video Series closely repeat achievements already covered in Work Experience.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs or use a label-plus-description format.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Make it sharper by foregrounding scope, platform leadership, and any measurable outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a clearer positioning line: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs like “Led,” “Built,” “Designed,” “Advised,” “Delivered.”
- Add metrics where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams supported, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements.
- Tighten phrasing, e.g.:
- “Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current wording repeats themes already covered in the summary/core competencies: governance, analytics, workflows, AI-enabled search.
- Specific projects like the microsite and AI search may duplicate the footer; keep this entry higher-level unless you add outcomes here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add team size, budget, reporting improvements, production volume, cost savings, or engagement gains from the studio/analytics work.
- Tighten softer phrasing: change “strengthened digital operations” to “implemented publishing governance, editorial standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo bullets unless framed here as building the in-house studio and scaling production capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution for advocacy, program and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show ownership and outcome: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media role.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the program, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic labels with sharper, leadership-oriented wording tied to recent work:  
  “• Enterprise digital strategy • Editorial governance and publishing operations • Cross-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Audience-centered content strategy”
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” or “content strategy” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Keep terminology consistent with the rest of the CV: use “governance,” “operations,” and “strategy” since those recur in recent roles.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with Director/Consultant experience; avoid repeating exact phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the more detailed “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize current strengths tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, higher-value phrases rather than a long tool list: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

- If accurate, swap generic terms for stronger phrasing like “enterprise CMS modernization” and “search/discovery experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JS/jQuery, API integrations, and Airtable already appear in “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the full stack here.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so keep it only if this section is shortened overall.

Suggested edit:

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS platforms or add light qualifiers that reflect actual depth and recency.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add concise context: **Drupal (enterprise modernization, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.
- If you want more impact, replace weaker/older tools with proficiency framing: **Drupal (advanced), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping the platform list in only one place.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating extra Drupal detail elsewhere unless adding a distinct qualifier here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus toward execution: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Development & Integration Tools.”
- Use cleaner, current phrasing: “HTML/CSS” instead of “HTML5 • CSS3”; keep “JavaScript,” drop version-style labels.
- Group by function for scanability: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “custom front-end implementation,” “serverless scripts,” or “deployment automation” rather than just listing tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations.” Consider removing those from one section.
- “Workflow automation” already appears elsewhere; GitHub Actions may be enough here without repeating broader automation language.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function to improve scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “used to support cross-team content operations, approvals, and campaign coordination”
- Cut weaker/older-feeling tools if needed for concision; keep the most relevant to current work first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap heavily; listing all four may feel redundant unless each is genuinely current/relevant.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform depth and audience-engagement systems rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/context to make it stronger: **Enterprise email campaign management, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, and member engagement**
- If space allows, combine into one line: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • newsletter operations, segmentation, and engagement workflows**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic email/newsletter management here; that is already covered in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 NACo experience.
- Don’t overstate automation here if Power Automate/Zapier already cover workflow tooling in a separate skills item.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, make it tighter, more tool-led, and reserve broader capabilities for experience bullets where impact can be quantified.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing**
- Replace **SEO** with **Google Search Console** if you want this to stay tool-specific; keep SEO as a competency elsewhere.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with nothing or with a platform already named; dashboarding is an output, not a tool.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recently used tools: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This line substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping detail in one place only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating generic descriptors here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this entry is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content execution, and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Add measurable scope if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, channels supported, or team size.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; specify outcomes such as faster publishing, more consistent output, or expanded in-house production.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped formalize day-to-day publishing workflows while informally guiding a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around distinct contributions so it doesn’t blur with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the strongest differentiator: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Make the first sentence more specific and active: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with concrete outputs or channels if known.
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, projects supported, stakeholders served, or content produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital media roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad “supporting organizational programs and policy work” language if similar wording appears elsewhere; specify the function or audience.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item is a bit generic and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims elsewhere. Make it more tool-specific and operationally senior, with emphasis on current/recent capabilities.
